| [NOTE-1717](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1717.md) | Chen, Kuo, Liu, Poon, Towey, Tse and Zhou — Metamorphic testing: a review of challenges and opportunities | A review by metamorphic testing's originators. It defines metamorphic relations as necessary properties over two or more inputs and their outputs, says the method alleviates but cannot solve the oracle problem, and supplies three limits for using such relations as a scorer: they are necessary not sufficient, their choice dominates what is found, and their source decides whether passing them verifies or validates. | Read |

| [NOTE-1811](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1811.md) | Herrmannsdoerfer, Benz and Juergens — COPE - Automating Coupled Evolution of Metamodels and Models | When a modeling language's metamodel changes, the existing models must be migrated. The paper calls this pairing "coupled evolution". **The requirements study.** An earlier study of two industrial metamodel histories found: - about half the changes were metamodel-only; - more than three quarters of the coupled changes were metamodel-independent, so they could be reused; - the rest were metamodel-specific; - none were model-specific. This yields two requirements: reuse and expressiveness. **COPE's answer.** A language evolves through a sequence of coupled transactions, each pairing a metamodel adaptation with its model migration. | Read |
| [NOTE-1826](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1826.md) | Kephart and Chess — The vision of autonomic computing | A programmatic statement of IBM's autonomic-computing agenda: computing systems that manage themselves "given high-level objectives from administrators". It sets out four aspects of self-management (configuration, optimization, healing, protection), proposes that autonomic systems be collections of autonomic elements each consisting of managed elements and an autonomic manager, and lists engineering and scientific challenges: element life cycles, service relationships negotiated between elements, security and trust, the specification of goals by humans, emergent behaviour, robustness, multi-agent learning, negotiation theory and statistical modelling. The architectural picture later called MAPE-K, and an agenda. | Read |
